title: Lesson 2 Quiz: Saving, Interest, and Compound Growth
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: You deposit $800 in an account that pays 3% simple interest per year. You make no other deposits or withdrawals. How much interest, in dollars, do you earn in total over 4 years? (Enter a number only.)

Hypothetical example: $2,500 is deposited at 4% per year, compounded annually, for 2 years with no other deposits or withdrawals. What is the balance after 2 years, in dollars? Round to the nearest cent, and round only at the final step. (Enter a number only.)
Hypothetical example: Bank A pays a 4.00% APR compounded monthly. Bank B pays a 4.05% APY. Assuming no fees and the same safety, which account earns more over one year?

choices.text: Bank B, because 4.05% is higher than 4.00%
They earn the same, since both rates are close to 4%
Bank A, because its APY is about 4.07%
Bank B, because monthly compounding lowers the APY

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A savings account earns a nominal return of 6% over a year in which inflation is 4%. Using the exact formula (1 + nominal) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1, what is the real return, in percent? Round to two decimal places. (Enter a number only.)
Why is an emergency fund usually kept in an insured savings account (deposit insurance rules differ by country) rather than invested in the shares of a single company?

choices.text: Shares cannot be sold quickly, even in normal markets
It needs to be reachable quickly and keep a stable value
Savings accounts tend to earn higher returns than shares
Insured accounts protect the fund against inflation
